rubric.evidence: Every claim traces to a primary source fetched live on 2026-07-28: the explainer README was read in full (376 lines, saved locally), the ChromeStatus API record (OT stage: desktop/Android/WebView 151–155, trial name DeclarativePerformanceObserver, owner sisidovski@google.com, pre-incubation standards maturity), both blink-dev threads (Intent to Prototype 69f31432…, Intent to Experiment 6a6078b0… — TAG review pending verified in the OT thread body), and Chromium runtime_enabled_features.json5 (DeclarativePerformanceObserver, status experimental, origin_trial_feature_name set, follows OT). One unverifiable claim was caught and corrected before handoff: the explainer's TOC lists a 'Crash Detection Heuristic vs. Explicit Field' section that has no body content — the page now states that gap explicitly instead of inventing its conclusion. Malformed-header handling and the exact OT entry-types value set are documented as 'not specified in the explainer (2026-07-28)' rather than guessed.

Feature id 6594955352080384 appears in the v151 listing under 'Origin trial'; the slug derives from the listing name per the slug rule; the H1 is the listing name verbatim. Listing status (Origin trial), OT window (151–155 desktop/Android/WebView), and spec status (pre-incubation personal-repo explainer, WICG proposal #280 open, TAG pending) are presented as separate facts, not conflated.

Nine inventory items cover the whole feature surface: the Performance-Observer header, its four directives (report-to, entry-types, include-user-timing, capture-early-failures), the report payload format, PerformanceSessionEndTiming, the early-failure capture/deferred-reporting lifecycle, and the session activation/termination/deactivation lifecycle. Each item maps all nine contract dimensions to rendered fragments (validate-artifacts clean for this id). Two child routes (performance-observer-header/, performancesessionendtiming/) carry the deep reference; the overview carries payload, lifecycle, compat, and security.

The lede states the mental model (declarative header activation + browser-process collection + Reporting API delivery at session end). 'why it exists' names the three concrete data-loss classes from the explainer (early network failures, OOM/abrupt termination, session end) and the mechanism that fixes them (out-of-band streaming so a renderer kill cannot take recorded data with it). Explicit non-goals (not a PerformanceObserver/NEL/crash-reporting replacement) are stated. Design decisions are explained with the explainer's own rationale (header allowlist vs markOptions; explicit terminal entry vs spec minimalism; endpoint non-persistence).

Header configuration (minimal + full), Reporting-Endpoints pairing, performance.mark() with detail passthrough, and a full annotated report payload are all shown as semantic pre/code blocks drawn from the explainer's worked examples. No live demo is possible: the feature is server-side header configuration behind an origin trial, the CPS showcase route 404s (verified and stated on-page), and local Chrome is not a 151+ OT-registered build, so runtime behavior is documented from sources, not executed.

No BCD entry and no webstatus.dev web-feature exist (both queried 2026-07-28, queries linked on-page), so the interim table is built from linked primary sources: Chrome/Edge OT 151–155 (ChromeStatus API record + Intent to Experiment), Firefox and Safari 'No signal' (ChromeStatus vendor views, no position recorded), and an explicit WPT row (no declarative-performance-observer directory or test upstream; performance-timeline suite covers only the imperative API). The Baseline banner says 'Limited availability' honestly. Unknown is stated as unknown rather than implied unsupported.

All 53 unique external hrefs across the three pages were curl-verified 2026-07-28: 52 return 200; the single 404 is the CPS showcase route, which is linked deliberately alongside text stating it returns 404 (documenting the demo's absence). Every named source links separately to its canonical original (per-section explainer anchors, spec anchors, both intent msgids, crbug, WICG #280, runtime_enabled_features.json5). Zero plain-text source labels; all external links use target=_blank rel=noopener.

Single main and h1 per page; sequential h1→h2 outline; all tables use th scope=row for row-header reference rows or thead for column headers; the baseline banner is role=note with aria-label; crumbs navigation on every route; child routes cross-link back to overview sections.

Six full-page screenshots (390×844-class mobile and 1280×800 desktop for all three routes) were captured from the local server and read. One real defect was caught and fixed: the PerformanceSessionEndTiming H1 broke mid-token ('PerformanceSessionE/ndTiming') at 390px; <wbr> hints at component boundaries fixed it (textContent identical to the interface name). doc-tables use table-layout fixed + min-width 36rem inside .table-wrap overflow-x auto with overflow-wrap anywhere, pre blocks scroll internally; no document-level horizontal overflow at either size.

No CPS showcase route exists for this feature (https://chrome-platform-showcase.paulkinlan-ea.deno.net/v151/declarative-performance-observer/ returns 404, verified 2026-07-28), so the contract's text-fallback path was used: the examples section states the 404 explicitly and explains why a client-side demo frame cannot meaningfully demonstrate server-side header configuration. No iframe was fabricated and no sibling concept was repointed.

openQuestions: Runtime behavior is documented from the explainer, ChromeStatus, and Chromium source but was not executed: verifying end-to-end (serve header → receive application/reports+json POST → inspect zero-filled failure entries and the session-end entry) needs a Chrome 151+ build with an OT token or --enable-blink-features=DeclarativePerformanceObserver plus a local reporting endpoint.

The explainer does not pin down the exact entry-types value set honored during the origin trial (it says values match PerformanceObserver.supportedEntryTypes), nor malformed-header/malformed-directive handling; both are stated on-page as unspecified as of 2026-07-28.
The explainer's TOC lists a 'Crash Detection Heuristic vs. Explicit Field' section with no content; whether PerformanceSessionEndTiming will gain closure typing is an open design question.
TAG review is pending and WICG proposal #280 is open; the header grammar and payload format may change before any ship milestone.
